# Try skeletonization: iteratively remove boundary cells until reaching core
def find_skeleton(grid, target_color, max_iter=100):
    """Iteratively remove border/background-connected cells until converging to core"""
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    
    # Start with copy of foreground cells
    cells = set()
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            if grid[r][c] == target_color:
                cells.add((r, c))
    
    prev_len = len(cells) + 1
    iteration = 0
    
    while prev_len > len(cells) and iteration < max_iter:
        iteration += 1
        new_cells = set()
        
        for (r, c) in cells:
            # Count same-color neighbors
            n_neighbors = sum([
                (r-1, c) in cells,
                (r+1, c) in cells,
                (r, c-1) in cells,
                (r, c+1) in cells
            ])
            
            # Keep if has neighbors (not isolated)
            if n_neighbors > 0:
                new_cells.add((r, c))
        
        cells = new_cells
        prev_len = len(cells)
    
    return cells
